$comment: The $id is the raw file on the project's own repository, so it dereferences to this document. It is an identifier only — kit.json points at this schema by relative path, and nothing in the repo fetches the $id.
title: Kit Contract
description: The machine- and agent-readable contract every kit declares. Base skills and packs program ONLY against this contract, never against a concrete kit. See base/README.md for the boundary rules.

baseVersion.description: Semver of the base system this kit targets. Base stays on 0.x until a second kit validates the abstraction.

kitVersion.description: Semver of this kit's own release — the same number package.json carries, moving with it (verify-harness fails if the two disagree). Distinct from baseVersion, which tracks the agent-system layer on its own 0.x line.

commands.description: Named shell commands the agent invokes instead of guessing. install/serve/build/test/lint are the expected keys; a kit may add more.

healthChecks.description: Ordered checks with a plain-language description a non-developer can understand. /health runs these.

capabilities.description: What this kit can actually do: artifacts it can produce (file:, content:, page:), verifications it can run (check:) and changes it can make to the site itself (site:, e.g. site:make-it-yours — name the site, remove sample content). file:markdown is mandatory (the universal fallback). Content types are capabilities of the form content:<type>.

tools.description: Optional: the helper commands that provide capabilities, so a kit-blind skill finds HOW to do what `capabilities` says the kit CAN do. A skill reads the capability, looks up the entry whose `provides` holds it, runs `run --help` first, then for real.

run.description: The full command, e.g. node tools/pdf.mjs, so a skill never guesses a path.

provides.description: Capability ids this tool provides (each must also be listed in capabilities). May be empty for a helper that provides none.

description.description: What it is for, in plain language a non-developer understands.

designSystemDoc.description: Repo-relative path to the design-system doc the workshop (/dev/design) and component skills read.

onboardingExtraQuestions.description: Kit-specific questions the base /onboarding interview appends after its generic rounds.

options.description: For type choice: the answers the interview offers, in this order.

default.description: The answer written to the manifest, marked (default), when the question is skipped (the onboarding rule that skipping never leaves a hole): a string for text and choice (for choice, one of options), a boolean for boolean.
